subject: general
question: Which of the given tribal uprisings did NOT take place around the unrest during the Revolt of 1857?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Birsa Munda Revolt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Birsa Munda Revolt**, also known as the Ulgulan (The Great Tumult), occurred in the late 19th century (1899–1900) and was not connected to the Revolt of 1857.
 
• This revolt was led by **Birsa Munda**, a tribal leader from the Munda community, in the Chotanagpur region (present-day Jharkhand).
 
• The rebellion primarily aimed at resisting British colonial exploitation and missionary interference in tribal lands and culture.
 
• Birsa Munda's movement focused on the restoration of tribal rights over their land (Khuntkatti system) and rejecting oppressive British laws.
 
• Unlike the other uprisings mentioned, which were closely linked to the broader unrest during the Revolt of 1857, the Birsa Munda Revolt was a localized tribal movement in the late 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rebellion of Sambalpur (1857–1864):**

 
 
• This revolt was led by Veer Surendra Sai against British rule in Sambalpur (present-day Odisha).
 
• It was closely linked to the larger Revolt of 1857 and aimed at overthrowing British authority in the region.
 
• Surendra Sai fought for the restoration of local tribal and princely rights.
 
 
 
• **Naikda Movement (1857–1858):**
 
 
• This tribal uprising occurred in Gujarat during the Revolt of 1857.
 
• The Naikda tribe resisted British policies that disrupted their traditional lifestyle and autonomy.
 
• It was a localized movement but inspired by the general anti-colonial sentiment of 1857.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Rebellion (1855–1856):**
 
 
• Led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, the Santhal Rebellion took place in the Rajmahal Hills (present-day Jharkhand).
 
• It was a precursor to the Revolt of 1857 and aimed at resisting oppressive zamindari systems and British policies.
 
• The Santhal tribes fought for their rights to land and freedom from exploitative moneylenders.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Movements in India:**
 
 
• Tribal uprisings were often reactions to exploitation by British policies, zamindars, and moneylenders.
 
• Most tribal revolts were rooted in issues like land alienation, forced labor, and cultural interference.
 
• These movements highlight the resilience and struggles of indigenous communities against colonial oppression.
